workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(fetch): reject an invalid prompt URL with -32602. workarounds.symptom: Client never retries after -32020 HeaderMismatch, and there is no public way to pre-load the x-mcp-header map (SEP-2243 client SHOULD/MAY both unimplemented)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Retry a tool call once after a HeaderMismatch rejection. Target files: src/mcp/client/client.py, tests/docs_src/test_header_parameters.py, tests/interaction/_requirements.py. On a 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP connection, `Client.call_tool` for a tool with `x-mcp-header` arguments failed with `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) unless that client had already listed the tool. It also kept failing when the tool's schema gained an annotation after it was listed. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3627)

workarounds.symptom: test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape fails on Windows without elevation or Developer Mode
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fall back to an NTFS junction when the symlink escape test can't create a symlink. Target files: tests/shared/test_path_security.py. `test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape` called `symlink_to()` unguarded. Windows only allows that for elevated processes or with Developer Mode on, so on an ordinary Windows dev machine the test errored with `WinError 1314` before it ever reached `safe_join`. CI didn't notice because the hosted Windows runners are allowed to create symlinks. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3609)

workarounds.symptom: Client.listTools() silently drops pages when a server repeats a cursor
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(client): follow nextCursor until it is absent; stop on a repeated page. Target files: packages/client/src/client/client.ts, packages/client/test/client/responseCache.test.ts, .changeset/keep-next-cursor-on-early-stop.md. A bare `listTools()` / `listPrompts()` / `listResources()` / `listResourceTemplates()` call stopped its page walk as soon as the server sent a `nextCursor` it had sent before, and returned the short list silently with no `nextCursor`.
